data.source_title: Acute Care Utilization After Recovery Coaching Linkage During Substance-Related Inpatient Admission: Results of Two Randomized Controlled Trials
data.locator: Abstract, Key Results; recovery-support engagement over six months after discharge.
data.source_setting: Inpatient adults with substance use disorder at Greenville Memorial Hospital, Greenville, South Carolina; two parallel single-center randomized trials.
data.source_period: Recruitment April 2018-June 2019 (study 1) and July 2019-March 2020 (study 2); six-month follow-up.
data.quantity: Engagement in recovery support services within six months post-discharge
data.unit: percent engaged in recovery support services
data.source_evidence_basis: Trial abstract reports higher self-reported recovery-support engagement for intervention vs control (84%, 95% CI 78-91; 34%, 95% CI 25-44; p<.001). Combined two-trial full text inspected.
data.limitations: Single-center pilot-trial setting; engagement outcome does not establish reduced overall acute-care use or clinical improvement. Not a psychiatric ED boarding endpoint and not RWJ data.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Represent inpatient addiction consultation/recovery-coach contact and post-discharge linkage as explicit transitions, with follow-up engagement measured separately from readmission or symptom outcomes. Do not assume this effect size locally.
